sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日简报 DealBook 的商业与政策报道。

sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市的 DealBook 峰会上，与商业、政治和文化领域一些极具影响力的人物进行现场对谈，其中包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·

sentences.en: Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经过滤的对话。

sentences.zh: 我们将对部分访谈进行现场直播，任何人都可以于11月

sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序来观看，并免费获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天。

sentences.en: Democrats are working on an election strategy for the midterms and beyond.
sentences.zh: 民主党人正在制定中期选举及以后的选举策略。

sentences.en: Why it deliberately sounds less ambitious than it is.
sentences.zh: 为什么它刻意听起来没有那么雄心勃勃。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, July 31St.
sentences.zh: 今天是7月31日，星期二。

sentences.en: Hi, how are you?
sentences.zh: 嗨，你好吗？

sentences.en: I'm well, and yourself?
sentences.zh: 我很好，你呢？

sentences.en: Good, good, good.
sentences.zh: 很好，很好，很好。

sentences.en: I think we're trying to connect with the congressman.
sentences.zh: 我想我们正在尝试联系国会议员。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，好的。

sentences.en: Are you from the New York Times?
sentences.zh: 你是《纽约时报》的吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes, hi there, congressman.
sentences.zh: 是的，你好，议员。

sentences.en: It's Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: Hey, how are you doing?
sentences.zh: 嘿，你好吗？

sentences.en: I'm doing really, really well.
sentences.zh: 我真的非常非常好。

sentences.en: Thank you very much for making some time for us.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你抽出时间接受我们的采访。

sentences.en: Well, it's great to be on with you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能和你们一起交流。

sentences.en: Look forward to our conversation.
sentences.zh: 期待我们的对话。

sentences.en: Me too.
sentences.zh: 我也是。

sentences.en: So, Conkerton, the reason why we're talking to you today is because there's this sense that the Democratic Party has lost its way.
sentences.zh: 那么，康克顿，我们今天找你谈话的原因是，人们有一种感觉，即民主党已经迷失了方向。

sentences.en: Do you think that the Democratic Party is lost?
sentences.zh: 你认为民主党迷失了吗？

sentences.en: I definitely don't think that we've been lost, as some have indicated.
sentences.zh: 我绝对不认为我们像某些人所说的那样迷失了方向。

sentences.en: I do think that
sentences.zh: 我确实认为

sentences.en: 2016 election was a shock to the system for a lot of folks, and there was an expectation that Hillary
sentences.zh: 2016年大选对许多人来说是一次体制上的震动，当时人们期望希拉里·

sentences.en: Clinton was going to be successful, and perhaps we were going to be able to take back the Senate, if not the House of Representatives.
sentences.zh: 克林顿会获胜，也许我们能够夺回参议院，即使不是众议院的话。

sentences.en: And the fact that we came into the 115th Congress with Donald
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们在唐纳德·

sentences.en: Trump as president and Republican majorities in the House and the Senate has forced us as Democrats
sentences.zh: 特朗普担任总统以及共和党在参众两院占据多数的情况下进入第115届国会，这迫使我们民主党人

sentences.en: to reevaluate how we govern and how we communicate what we stand for to the American people.
sentences.zh: 重新评估我们的施政方式，以及如何向美国人民阐明我们的立场。

sentences.en: But you don't think the party has lost its way?
sentences.zh: 但你不认为党迷失了方向吗？

sentences.en: Well, in my view, a setback is nothing more than a setup for a comeback.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，挫折不过是东山再起的垫脚石。

sentences.en: And we certainly experienced a significant setback.
sentences.zh: 我们确实经历了一次重大的挫折。

sentences.en: But that has allowed us as Democrats to make sure that we both reevaluate how we communicate to the American people, and more significantly, to clarify what we stand for.
sentences.zh: 但这让我们民主党人得以确保两件事：一是重新评估我们与美国人民的沟通方式，更重要的是，明确我们的主张。

sentences.en: Coming out of the 2016 election, we needed to make it clear that there was a blind spot that we had
sentences.zh: 经历2016年大选后，我们需要明确指出，作为民主党人，我们在

sentences.en: as Democrats with respect to engaging with the American people around the economic anxiety that
sentences.zh: 回应美国人民持续感受到的经济焦虑方面存在盲区，

sentences.en: they continue to experience, notwithstanding the tremendous progress that was made during the eight years of Barack Obama's presidency.
sentences.zh: 尽管在巴拉克·奥巴马八年总统任期内取得了巨大的进步。

sentences.en: Alex Burns, I wanted to talk to you because heading into the midterms, we've been trying to figure out what the Democratic Party's plan is and whether they have a plan.
sentences.zh: 亚历克斯·伯恩斯，我想和你聊聊，因为在临近中期选举之际，我们一直在试图弄清楚民主党人的计划是什么，以及他们是否真的有计划。

sentences.en: So I recently had a conversation with Congressman Hakeem Jeffries, who is an up-and-coming member of
sentences.zh: 所以我最近采访了众议员哈基姆·杰弗里斯，他是

sentences.en: the House and one of the people tasked with figuring out the Democratic Party's plan.
sentences.zh: 众议院的新星，也是负责制定民主党计划的人之一。

sentences.en: But the plan that he outlined in our conversation seemed confusingly narrow to me.
sentences.zh: 但在我们的对话中，他概述的计划在我看来窄得令人困惑。

sentences.en: So I wanted to talk to you to understand, is it narrow?
sentences.zh: 所以我特来与你探讨：它真的很窄吗？

sentences.en: Do the Democrats have a good plan?
sentences.zh: 民主党人有一个好计划吗？

sentences.en: And do they understand their problems?
sentences.zh: 他们了解自己的问题吗？

sentences.en: So I guess my first question is, what is the problem with the Democratic Party?
sentences.zh: 我想我的第一个问题是，民主党的问题到底出在哪里？

sentences.en: Well, to answer that question, we probably need to back up about a decade to when Barack Obama comes into office after the 2008 election.
sentences.zh: 嗯，要回答这个问题，我们大概需要把时间倒回大约十年前，也就是2008年大选后巴拉克·奥巴马就职的时候。

sentences.en: We still doubt that America is a place where all things are possible.
sentences.zh: 我们依然坚信美国是一个一切皆有可能的地方。

sentences.en: Democrats have control of the House.
sentences.zh: 民主党控制了众议院。

sentences.en: They have control of the Senate.
sentences.zh: 他们控制了参议院。

sentences.en: They have sweeping control of governorships around the country, as good as it's gotten for them, certainly in our lifetimes.
sentences.zh: 他们在全国范围内对州长职位拥有压倒性的控制，这可以说是我们有生以来他们取得过的最好局面。

sentences.en: And they make a series of political choices that have drastic implications.
sentences.zh: 而他们做出了一系列政治选择，产生了深远的影响。

sentences.en: And they're basically still grappling with the fallout from that election today.
sentences.zh: 直到今天，他们基本上仍在努力应对那场选举带来的余波。

sentences.en: What were the choices that they made that we're still grappling with?
sentences.zh: 他们究竟作出了哪些我们至今仍在应对的选择？

sentences.en: Well, the biggest choice that Democrats made after 2008 was to pursue a national health care law with their total control of government.
sentences.zh: 嗯，2008年后民主党人做出的最大选择，就是凭借对政府的全面控制，推行一项全国性的医疗保健法案。

sentences.en: But we did not come here just to clean up crises.
sentences.zh: 但我们来这里不只是为了收拾烂摊子。

sentences.en: We came here to build a future.
sentences.zh: 我们来这里是为了建设未来。

sentences.en: So tonight, I return to speak to all of you about an issue that is central to that future.
sentences.zh: 因此，今晚我再次与大家交谈，探讨一个对该未来至关重要的问题。

sentences.en: And that is the issue of health care.
sentences.zh: 那就是医疗保健问题。

sentences.en: If you think of the total political capital that Obama came into office with, and the share of it that he spent on health care alone, it's overwhelming.
sentences.zh: 如果你想想奥巴马刚上台时拥有的全部政治资本，以及他单在医疗保健上花掉的比例，那是极其巨大的。

sentences.en: And if you look at the political implications of that, there's the obvious one, which is that
sentences.zh: 如果你看看其中的政治影响，有一个显而易见的事实，那就是

sentences.en: Republicans rode backlash against Obamacare to control of the House and then later the Senate.
sentences.zh: 共和党人借助对“奥巴马医改”的反弹控制了众议院，随后又控制了参议院。

sentences.en: But there's also a whole range of other issues that Democrats didn't deal with because they chose to focus on health care.
sentences.zh: 但由于他们选择专注于医疗保健，还有一系列其他问题是民主党人根本没有处理的。

sentences.en: They didn't do an immigration bill that could have meaningfully changed the nature of the American electorate over time.
sentences.zh: 他们没有推动一项本可以随着时间推移实质性改变美国选民结构性质的移民法案。

sentences.en: Well, if they had passed a liberal immigration bill with a pathway to citizenship for people who
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果他们通过了一项开辟入籍途径的自由派移民法案，让那些

sentences.en: are currently in the country illegally, you could have millions of people becoming eligible,
sentences.zh: 目前非法滞留国内的人有机会入籍，那么数以百万计的人可能会具备资格，

sentences.en: at least, for citizenship and voting rights, who in 2008 had no pathway there and still today have no pathway there.
sentences.zh: 至少可以获得公民身份和投票权——而在2008年他们没有通往这一目标的途径，直到今天也依然没有。

sentences.en: They didn't do that.
sentences.zh: 他们没有这么做。

sentences.en: They didn't do a national labor law to really, really strengthen labor unions.
sentences.zh: 他们没有制定一项真正、真正能够加强工会的全国劳工法。

sentences.en: That could have made an enormous difference for the Democratic
sentences.zh: 那本可以为密歇根州、俄亥俄州和宾夕法尼亚州等地的民主党

sentences.en: Party in places like Michigan and Ohio and Pennsylvania, the places that we now think of in many cases as Trump country.
sentences.zh: 带来巨大的改变，而这些地方现在很多都被我们视为特朗普的腹地。

sentences.en: The Democrats also didn't pursue any kind of national voting rights law.
sentences.zh: 民主党人也没有追求任何形式的全国投票权法案。

sentences.en: When you see issues like voter purges pop up in places like Ohio and North Carolina that matter
sentences.zh: 当你看到选民名单清洗等问题在俄亥俄州和北卡罗来纳州这样极为关键的

sentences.en: an enormous amount, these are issues that a federal voting law could actually have done something about.
sentences.zh: 地方出现时，联邦投票法其实是完全可以解决这些问题的。

sentences.en: Democrats did not make a real attempt to do that.
sentences.zh: 民主党人并没有为此做出真正的尝试。

sentences.en: So not giving citizenship to undocumented immigrants, not organizing labor in a systematic way, not enfranchising voters in a kind of permanent structural way.
sentences.zh: 所以，不给无证移民公民身份，不以系统化的方式组织劳工，不以某种永久性的结构方式赋予选民权利。

sentences.en: We're talking about potentially millions and millions of theoretically almost guaranteed Democratic votes not realized under the presidency of Barack Obama.
sentences.zh: 我们在谈论的是在巴拉克·奥巴马总统任期内未能实现的、潜在的数百万理论上几乎可以说是铁定的民主党选票。

sentences.en: That's certainly how the critics of the Obama presidency within the
sentences.zh: 民主党内部

sentences.en: Democratic Party see things.
sentences.zh: 奥巴马总统任期的批评者们显然就是这么看的。

sentences.en: And there are more of those people than you see in public because, look, across the Democratic Party, there is really still reverence for Barack Obama.
sentences.zh: 这样的人比你在公开场合看到的要多，因为你看，在整个民主党内部，对巴拉克·奥巴马的敬仰确实依然存在。

sentences.en: But there is this recognition that when Republicans have had power, they work very, very hard to expand and cement that power.
sentences.zh: 但人们也认识到，当共和党人掌权时，他们非常非常努力地去扩大和巩固这种权力。

sentences.en: And that's not something the Democrats saw Barack Obama do.
sentences.zh: 而这并不是民主党人在巴拉克·奥巴马身上看到的操作。

sentences.en: It sounds like as noble as it might seem, Obama focused on governing as a Democratic president, but not on building up the Democratic Party itself.
sentences.zh: 听起来，不管看起来多么崇高，奥巴马专注于作为一名民主党总统进行统治，而不是去壮大民主党本身。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And he focused on areas of governing that didn't do much to change the basic structures of American politics in a way that favored his own party.
sentences.zh: 他专注于那些对改变美国政治基本结构、从而对他的政党有利没有太大帮助的施政领域。

sentences.en: A great example of that is that when after the 2010 elections, Republicans in state capitals around the country redrew the
sentences.zh: 一个很好的例子是，在2010年中期选举之后，全国各州首府的共和党人重新划分了

sentences.en: congressional maps and state legislative maps in their own favor, the Obama Justice Department mostly did not challenge those maps in court.
sentences.zh: 国会选区地图和州立法选区地图以对自己有利，而奥巴马司法部基本上没有在法庭上对这些地图提出挑战。

sentences.en: You have seen the attorney general at the time,
sentences.zh: 你已经看到当时的司法部长

sentences.en: Eric Holder, has since been suing states all over the country.
sentences.zh: 埃里克·霍尔德此后一直在起诉全国各地的州。

sentences.en: He didn't do that when he was attorney general.
sentences.zh: 他在担任司法部长时可没有这么做。

sentences.en: The Obama administration let that one go.
sentences.zh: 奥巴马政府把这件事放过去了。

sentences.en: So that's fascinating.
sentences.zh: 这太迷人了。

sentences.en: I think we expect to start the clock of the Democratic problems in 2016 with the defeat of what seemed like a very well positioned Democratic nominee Hillary Clinton
sentences.zh: 我认为我们习惯于将民主党问题的起点定在2016年，当时看似占据极好优势的民主党候选人希拉里·克林顿

sentences.en: against a highly unconventional Republican candidate Donald Trump and everything that was revealed by that victory.
sentences.zh: 输给了一个极其非传统的共和党候选人唐纳德·特朗普，以及这场胜利所揭示的一切。

sentences.en: We see that as being where the problems start for the Democratic Party.
sentences.zh: 我们将此视为民主党问题开始的地方。

sentences.en: But you're saying that's not quite right?
sentences.zh: 但你是说这并不完全正确？

sentences.en: No, it's not.
sentences.zh: 不，不是的。

sentences.en: And when you look at the 2016 election, Democrats were already a clear minority in the House of Representatives, in the Senate, and in state capitals around the country.
sentences.zh: 当你回顾2016年大选时，民主党人在众议院、参议院以及全国各地的州首府已经明显处于少数地位。

sentences.en: When you're a party in that position, and you've essentially bet all your chips on the presidency
sentences.zh: 当你是一个处于这种地位的政党，并且基本上把所有的筹码都压在总统职位上

sentences.en: as a way to maintain a hand in government, you're not looking at a healthy political party.
sentences.zh: 作为维持政府话语权的方式时，你面对的就不是一个健康的政党。

sentences.en: So is the 2016 election, Alex, a symptom of this root problem, this kind of structural trouble you're talking about, an exacerbation of it, or what exactly?
sentences.zh: 那么亚历克斯，2016年大选是这个根本问题的症状，是你所说的这种结构性麻烦的加剧，还是究竟是什么？

sentences.en: I think it's the climax of it that you see in the 2016 election, the Democratic Party pay this catastrophic price.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是它的高潮，你在2016年大选中看到民主党付出了灾难性的代价。

sentences.en: So you saw Hillary Clinton lose and lose badly in places like Ohio and Iowa, where President Obama had won four years before and eight years before.
sentences.zh: 所以你看到希拉里·克林顿在俄亥俄州和艾奥瓦州等地惨败，而奥巴马总统在四年前和八年前曾赢得过这些地方。

sentences.en: What you saw in the intervening years is the Democratic Party, rather than trying to take care of its foundation in these
sentences.zh: 你在随后的几年里看到的是，民主党人没有去努力稳固他们在这些

sentences.en: places, you saw them embrace this theory that the country was changing so much, that there were
sentences.zh: 地方的根基，而是接受了这样一种理论：国家正在发生巨大变化，

sentences.en: generational and social and demographic changes in the country that sort of meant that they were inexorably going to win in 2016.
sentences.zh: 国内存在世代、社会和人口结构的变化，这某种程度上意味着他们在2016年将不可避免地获胜。

sentences.en: And you saw in the Clinton campaign, an entity that wanted the country to look like a state like Virginia, that was growing increasingly diverse.
sentences.zh: 你在克林顿的竞选团队中看到，这样一个实体希望国家看起来像弗吉尼亚州那样日益多元化。

sentences.en: And instead, you have a country that actually looks a lot more like Ohio, where she lost and lost badly.
sentences.zh: 然而取而代之的是，这个国家实际上看起来更像俄亥俄州，而她在那里遭遇了惨败。

sentences.en: And what does it mean to look like Ohio?
sentences.zh: 看起来像俄亥俄州意味着什么？

sentences.en: It means that you're looking at a state where there are very substantial minority communities, but they are not a decisive force in elections.
sentences.zh: 这意味着你看到的是这样一个州：那里有着相当可观的少数族裔社区，但他们在选举中并不是决定性力量。

sentences.en: You're looking at a community of white voters who are less college educated than the country at large, and where issues like trade, issues like
sentences.zh: 你看到的是一个白人选民社区，他们的大学教育水平低于全美平均水平，在那里，贸易问题、

sentences.en: immigration, issues like crime and policing play very differently than they do in the kinds of places where Hillary Clinton won.
sentences.zh: 移民问题、犯罪和治安问题所起到的作用，与希拉里·克林顿获胜的那些地方截然不同。

sentences.en: So I have, ever since the first day of my campaign, called for criminal justice reform.
sentences.zh: 因此，自竞选第一天起，我就呼吁进行刑事司法改革。

sentences.en: I've laid out a platform that I think would begin to remedy some of the problems we have in the criminal justice system.
sentences.zh: 我提出了一个纲领，我认为它将开始纠正我们在刑事司法系统中遇到的一些问题。

sentences.en: It's not just that the Clinton campaign is speaking to elites, it's that the people they're speaking
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是克林顿竞选团队在与精英对话，而是那些不是精英的受访者

sentences.en: to who aren't elites aren't necessarily hearing a message about the economy or about national security or about national identity that they find compelling.
sentences.zh: 不一定能听到他们觉得引人注目的关于经济、国家安全或国家认同的信息。

sentences.en: And we all want a society that is tolerant, inclusive, and fair.
sentences.zh: 我们都想要一个宽容、包容和公正的社会。

sentences.en: We all believe that America succeeds when more people share in our prosperity.
sentences.zh: 我们都坚信，当更多人分享我们的繁荣时，美国才会成功。

sentences.en: So you had people start to think that the Democratic Party was not talking to them anymore.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们开始觉得民主党不再同他们对话了。

sentences.en: And in 2016, they didn't necessarily get a message from Hillary Clinton that sounded like even the message they got from Barack Obama four years earlier.
sentences.zh: 在2016年，他们从希拉里·克林顿那里得到的信息，甚至听起来都不如四年前从巴拉克·奥巴马那里听到的信息。

sentences.en: And then, of course, in walks Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 然后，当然，唐纳德·特朗普登场了。

sentences.en: And in walks Donald Trump, who is probably unique among modern Republicans as somebody who would speak the populist language that Democrats had talked for generations.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普登场了，他在现代共和党人中大概是独一无二的，他会用民主党人讲了几代人的民粹主义语言说话。

sentences.en: The forgotten men and women won't be forgotten anymore.
sentences.zh: 被遗忘的男男女女将不再被遗忘。

sentences.en: Forgotten men and women.
sentences.zh: 被遗忘的男男女女。

sentences.en: I see you, I hear you, and I will never, ever let you down, I promise.
sentences.zh: 我看到你们，我听得到你们，我向你们保证，我绝不会、绝不会让你们失望。

sentences.en: We will never let you down.
sentences.zh: 我们绝不会让你们失望。

sentences.en: He goes into a place like Michigan, which rejected George W.
sentences.zh: 他去了像密歇根州这样曾两次拒绝乔治·W·

sentences.en: Bush twice, and he wins it.
sentences.zh: 布什的地方，并赢得了那里。

sentences.en: And Democrats, in between the 2004 election and the 2016 election, had kind of convinced themselves that these states belong to us.
sentences.zh: 在2004年大选和2016年大选之间，民主党人曾某种程度上说服自己，这些州是属于我们的。

sentences.en: And they hadn't done a lot of the work that it would require to make sure that that state stays locked down.
sentences.zh: 他们并没有做很多工作来确保这个州万无一失。

sentences.en: Do the Democrats understand all of this?
sentences.zh: 民主党人明白这一切吗？

sentences.en: That the problem doesn't just start and stop with Hillary Clinton and Donald Trump, but that they have a bigger problem on their hands.
sentences.zh: 明白这个问题并不止于希拉里·克林顿和唐纳德·特朗普，而是他们手头面临着一个更大的问题。

sentences.en: And that's why they've lost control.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们失控的原因。

sentences.en: For the most part, they do understand it.
sentences.zh: 大多数情况下，他们确实明白了。

sentences.en: And that's why in 2018, you see them focusing so narrowly on a couple places in the political map where they think they
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么在2018年，你会看到他们如此狭隘地聚焦于政治版图上的几个地方，他们认为

sentences.en: can start to claw their way back in state capitals, and most importantly, in the House of Representatives.
sentences.zh: 自己可以在那里开始在州首府、以及最重要地在众议院夺回一席之地。

sentences.en: So that brings us back to my conversation with Hakeem Jeffries.
sentences.zh: 这就把我们带回了我与哈基姆·杰弗里斯的对话。

sentences.en: So let me explain a couple of things that confused me about talking to him.
sentences.zh: 让我解释一下关于与他交谈让我感到困惑的几点。

sentences.en: First of all, you just used the word narrow, and his plan, to my mind, felt incredibly narrow.
sentences.zh: 首先，你刚才用了“狭隘”这个词，而在我看来，他的计划确实感到不可思议地狭隘。

sentences.en: There was an absence of a clear and compelling message that dealt with the economic anxieties of the American people.
sentences.zh: 当时缺乏一个清晰且引人注目、能够直面美国民众经济焦虑的信息。

sentences.en: But we as House Democrats, looking forward, decided that we were going to make sure we corrected that problem.
sentences.zh: 但我们作为众议院的民主党人，在展望未来时，决定确保我们纠正这个问题。

sentences.en: And that's what initially gave birth to the Better Deal economic agenda, focused on better jobs, better wages, and a better future, higher pay, lower costs,
sentences.zh: 这也是“更好交易”经济议程最初诞生的原因，该议程聚焦于更好的工作、更好的工资和更美好的未来、更高的薪酬、更低的成本，

sentences.en: and making sure the American people had the tools to succeed in the 21st century economy.
sentences.zh: 并确保美国人民拥有在21世纪经济中取得成功的工具。

sentences.en: And I think we've done a reasonably good job of staying focused on economic issues that are
sentences.zh: 而且我认为我们在专注于经济议题方面做得相当不错，这些议题

sentences.en: important to get us to the point where we're now in striking distance to finish the job and win back the House in November.
sentences.zh: 对于让我们走到现在这一步至关重要，我们现在距离完成工作并在11月夺回众议院只有一步之遥。

sentences.en: It's a plan just for the House, he said, not for the Senate and not even for the candidates seeking a seat in the House.
sentences.zh: 他说，这是一个仅针对众议院的计划，不针对参议院，甚至不针对寻求众议院席位的候选人。

sentences.en: And that seems like a recipe for disaster if people are looking for a clear identity for the entire Democratic Party.
sentences.zh: 如果人们在寻找整个民主党清晰的身份认同，这看起来就像是一个灾难的配方。

sentences.en: I don't think most voters distinguish between Democrats in the House and Democrats in the Senate or even a Democratic presidential candidate.
sentences.zh: 我认为大多数选民不会区分众议院的民主党人和参议院的民主党人，甚至民主党总统候选人。

sentences.en: So am I wrong to think that that plan seems quite narrow?
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我认为那个计划显得相当狭隘，我是错的吗？

sentences.en: No, it is really narrow.
sentences.zh: 不，它确实很狭隘。

sentences.en: And it's a matter of political necessity for Democrats that they campaign in a fairly narrow way.
sentences.zh: 对于民主党人来说，以相当狭隘的方式开展竞选是一个政治上的必要问题。

sentences.en: This is about the House of Representatives because the House is the place where Democrats think they can actually start to win back power.
sentences.zh: 这关乎众议院，因为众议院是民主党人认为他们实际上可以开始夺回权力的地方。

sentences.en: Very, very tough to imagine them taking the Senate this year.
sentences.zh: 要想象他们今年拿下参议院，真是难上加难。

sentences.en: Not impossible, but very tough.
sentences.zh: 并非不可能，但非常艰难。

sentences.en: So you see them focusing on the House because they think if they can start to win some places that have historically voted for Republicans
sentences.zh: 所以你可以看到他们把重点放在众议院，因为他们认为如果他们能开始赢得一些历史上投票支持共和党的地方，

sentences.en: and some places that voted for Donald Trump, then they can use the House to position the party in a much more politically appealing way than the Clinton campaign did in 2016.
sentences.zh: 以及一些投票给唐纳德·特朗普的地方，那么他们就可以利用众议院将党派定位在一个比2016年克林顿竞选团队更具政治吸引力的立场上。

sentences.en: So the map for taking back the House supports a plan that's focused on voters that they realize they kind of neglected in 2016.
sentences.zh: 因此，夺回众议院的战略蓝图支持这样一项计划，即把重点放在那些他们意识到在2016年有些忽视的选民身上。

sentences.en: It's focused on voters who are soft Republican voters.
sentences.zh: 它聚焦于那些温和的共和党选民。

sentences.en: Well, the economic issues are what are unifying as it relates to the gorgeous mosaic of the American people.
sentences.zh: 嗯，说到美国人民这幅绚丽的马赛克，经济议题正是最具凝聚力的部分。

sentences.en: Sort of when we decide to communicate clearly about what we as Democrats stand for, for the people.
sentences.zh: 就像我们决定明确传达我们作为民主党人代表什么、为人民争取什么一样。

sentences.en: We're talking about urban America, rural America, suburban America, the heartland, small-town America, the north, the south, the east, and the weSt.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的是城市美国、乡村美国、郊区美国、心脏地带、小镇美国、北方、南方、东方和西方。

sentences.en: You're talking about people who voted for Trump, voted for him reluctantly, maybe didn't like him on the day that they voted for him but didn't like Hillary Clinton.
sentences.zh: 你谈论的是那些投票给特朗普的人、勉强投票给他的人、可能在投票给他的那天并不喜欢他但又讨厌希拉里·克林顿的人。

sentences.en: People who might have been
sentences.zh: 那些可能曾经是

sentences.en: Democrats in 2008 and sometime in the middle drifted away from the party.
sentences.zh: 2008年的民主党人，在中间某个时候逐渐疏离了党派的人。

sentences.en: And so what you see in the messaging from Democrats, at least the Democrats who are campaigning effectively, is you see them
sentences.zh: 所以你在民主党人的传达的信息中看到的是，至少那些竞选行之有效的民主党人，你会看到他们

sentences.en: talking about issues that will appeal to a 60-year-old white guy who's a union member in Toledo
sentences.zh: 在谈论能够吸引托莱多的一名工会成员、60岁白人男性

sentences.en: and a white woman who makes six figures as a lawyer in the suburbs of Columbus and small donors to the
sentences.zh: 以及哥伦布郊区一位年薪六位数的白人女性的议题，还有来自

sentences.en: Democratic Party in places like New York and Los Angeles and San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 纽约、洛杉矶和旧金山等地的民主党小额捐赠者。

sentences.en: And there aren't that many issues that cut across all three of those groups.
sentences.zh: 能够同时切中这三个群体的议题并不多。

sentences.en: We've articulated three issues that we're going to focus on in terms of improving the quality of life of everyday Americans.
sentences.zh: 我们已经明确了三个议题，我们将围绕这些议题来提高普通美国人的生活质量。

sentences.en: Number one, we're going to lower health care costs.
sentences.zh: 第一，我们将降低医疗保健成本。

sentences.en: We're going to strengthen the Affordable Care Act.
sentences.zh: 我们将加强《平价医疗法案》。

sentences.en: We're going to dramatically drive down the price of prescription drugs.
sentences.zh: 我们将大幅压低处方药的价格。

sentences.en: Number two, we're going to focus on increasing the pay of everyday Americans with an emphasis on continued and strong economic growth by rebuilding America.
sentences.zh: 第二，我们将专注于通过重建美国来提高普通美国人的薪酬，并强调持续强劲的经济增长。

sentences.en: And number three, we're going to clean up corruption in Washington to make sure that government works for everyday
sentences.zh: 第三，我们将清理华盛顿的腐败，以确保政府为普通

sentences.en: Americans.
sentences.zh: 美国人服务。

sentences.en: And so that's what we're all about.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们存在的意义。

sentences.en: That's what Democrats wake up and fight for, right, for everyday Americans, for the people.
sentences.zh: 这就是民主党人醒来后为之奋斗的目标，为了普通美国人，为了人民。

sentences.en: And we've brought that to life through those three direct, distinct policy areas.
sentences.zh: 我们通过这三个直接、鲜明的政策领域将这一点付诸现实。

sentences.en: Does that explain why Hakeem Jeffers is talking about the economy, the economy, the economy, and nothing else?
sentences.zh: 这是否能解释为什么哈基姆·杰弗里斯一直在谈论经济、经济、经济，而没有别的？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And the idea is don't talk about those polarizing questions of identity, immigration, foreign policy, that that's counterproductive.
sentences.zh: 其核心理念是不要谈论身份认同、移民、外交政策这些两极分化的议题，因为那是适得其反的。

sentences.en: Or at least don't put them out front on the billboard that defines the Democratic Party.
sentences.zh: 或者至少不要把它们放在定义民主党形象的巨幅广告牌最显眼的位置。

sentences.en: There's never been a conversation amongst House Democrats about targeting any one particular group of folks.
sentences.zh: 众议院的民主党人从未讨论过针对任何特定群体。

sentences.en: It's about how do we reach everyday Americans and make sure that we are clearly articulating our focus and what we're about versus what they're about.
sentences.zh: 关键在于我们如何接触普通美国人，并确保我们清晰地阐述我们的重点以及我们的立场，与他们的立场形成对比。

sentences.en: If I could just call back to the 2010 election, Republicans did a similar thing with a message that at the time seemed to me to be fairly vapid, that you had this mantra that was,
sentences.zh: 如果我回想一下2010年的选举，共和党人做过类似的事情，当时传达的信息在我看来相当空洞，当时你们有这样一个口号：

sentences.en: where are the jobs?
sentences.zh: 工作在哪里？

sentences.en: It was not an agenda.
sentences.zh: 这不是一个议程。

sentences.en: It was really almost a taunt.
sentences.zh: 这几乎是一种嘲弄。

sentences.en: And I wondered whether it would work.
sentences.zh: 我当时在想这是否会奏效。

sentences.en: And it worked and it worked spectacularly well.
sentences.zh: 结果它真的奏效了，而且取得了惊人的成功。

sentences.en: So the idea is to talk about the economy economy and issues related to the economy that basically everybody cares about.
sentences.zh: 所以我们的想法是谈论经济、经济以及与经济相关的、基本上每个人都关心的议题。

sentences.en: So they need to govern on those economic principles in a way that rebuilds the party identity as for working people.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们需要按照这些经济原则进行执政，以此重建该党作为工人阶级代言人的形象。

sentences.en: If Democrats were to implement this plan successfully, I think what you would see them do is take the
sentences.zh: 如果民主党人成功实施这项计划，我认为你会看到他们拿下

sentences.en: House of Representatives and then pass popular bills on health care, popular bills on taxes,
sentences.zh: 众议院，然后通过关于医疗保健的受欢迎法案、关于税收的受欢迎法案、

sentences.en: popular bills on drug prices that would then get sent up to the Senate, maybe probably controlled
sentences.zh: 关于药价的受欢迎法案，这些法案随后会被提交给可能由

sentences.en: by Republicans and knocked back or sent through the Senate if Democrats take the Senate and then
sentences.zh: 共和党控制的参议院并被否决，或者如果民主党夺回参议院就在参议院通过，然后

sentences.en: knocked back by the White House and essentially use the House as a platform to define what you would get if Democrats actually controlled the federal government.
sentences.zh: 被白宫否决，并本质上将众议院作为一个平台，来定义如果民主党真正控制联邦政府，你们会得到什么。

sentences.en: So even if they don't succeed in passing any of this legislation, the message itself becomes potent and symbolic, lays the groundwork for the next election.
sentences.zh: 因此，即使他们没有成功通过任何这些立法，信息本身也会变得强大而具有象征意义，为下一场选举奠定基础。

sentences.en: In a lot of ways, it is, again, mimicking the Republicans from a few years ago that when
sentences.zh: 在许多方面，这再次是在模仿几年前的共和党人，当年

sentences.en: Republicans took the House, they voted, it felt like every other day, on repealing the Affordable
sentences.zh: 共和党人夺取众议院后，他们似乎每隔一天就投票一次，

sentences.en: Care Act, even though they knew there was not a chance that it was going to be repealed when
sentences.zh: 要求废除《平价医疗法案》，尽管他们知道在

sentences.en: Barack Obama was president.
sentences.zh: 巴拉克·奥巴马担任总统期间，这根本没有被废除的可能。

sentences.en: But it defined them as the party that was against this unpopular legislation.
sentences.zh: 但它将他们定义为反对这项不受欢迎的立法的政党。

sentences.en: And if the Democrats do this successfully, it would challenge the idea of President Trump as the man of the people, because he might sit there and literally veto these bills.
sentences.zh: 如果民主党人成功做到这一点，它将挑战特朗普总统作为“人民的总统”的形象，因为他可能会坐在那里，字面意义上地否决这些法案。

sentences.en: And it would give people a second version of what being for the working class looks like beyond the Trump version.
sentences.zh: 这将为人们提供除了特朗普版本之外的、关于支持工人阶级意味着什么的第二种版本。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: If they were to start passing a middle class tax cut that raised taxes on rich people and the president vetoed it, you would then have every Democrat campaigning
sentences.zh: 如果他们开始通过一项针对富人增税的中产阶级减税法案而总统予以否决，那么每个民主党人在竞选时都会宣称：

sentences.en: on, we need to stand up to this guy who's only in it for the one percent, which would really undercut the image that President Trump has cultivated.
sentences.zh: 我们需要挺身而出，对抗这个只为百分之一富人服务的人，这将真正削弱特朗普总统精心树立的形象。

sentences.en: Okay, so there's a total logic, now that you've explained it, to this Hakeem Jeffries
sentences.zh: 好吧，既然你解释了，哈基姆·杰弗里斯的这个

sentences.en: House plan.
sentences.zh: 众议院计划完全合乎逻辑。

sentences.en: Double down on the economy in a Democratic House, send legislation up to a likely Republican Senate and president that champions the working class, have them potentially,
sentences.zh: 在民主党掌控的众议院加倍关注经济，向可能由共和党控制的参议院和总统提交捍卫工人阶级的立法，让他们可能地、

sentences.en: likely knock it down, then run against them on that message in 2020, and theoretically reclaim the Senate, theoretically reclaim the presidency, and the working class.
sentences.zh: 很可能会否决它，然后在2020年围绕这一信息与他们对抗，理论上夺回参议院，理论上夺回总统职位，以及工人阶级。

sentences.en: Theoretically is the key word here, but yes, that's the sort of long-term vision.
sentences.zh: “理论上”是这里的关键词，但是的，这就是那种长期愿景。

sentences.en: But a lot can go wrong, and a lot, frankly, has already gone wrong since they announced this messaging plan.
sentences.zh: 但很多事情可能会出差错，而且坦率地说，自从他们宣布这一宣传计划以来，已经有很多事情出错了。

sentences.en: Hmm, like what exactly?
sentences.zh: 嗯，具体指什么？

sentences.en: Well, it was not in the plan to be talking about abolishing ICE.
sentences.zh: 嗯，谈论废除移民及海关执法局（ICE）并不在计划之中。

sentences.en: We need to rebuild our immigration system from top to bottom, starting by replacing ICE with something that reflects our morality.
sentences.zh: 我们需要彻底重建我们的移民系统，首先是用能够反映我们道德的机构来取代ICE。

sentences.en: A hundred days before a midterm election, right?
sentences.zh: 在期中选举前一百天，对吧？

sentences.en: As Senate.
sentences.zh: 作为参议院。

sentences.en: As prominent members of the Senate, some members of the House, activists around the country have been talking about it.
sentences.zh: 作为参议院的杰出成员、众议院的一些成员以及全国各地的活动人士一直在讨论的事情。

sentences.en: That puts pressure on Democrats in red districts, in purple districts, to address an issue that they simply don't want to be talking about, period.
sentences.zh: 这给处于红色选区、紫色选区的民主党人带来了压力，迫使他们去应对一个他们根本不想谈论的议题，句号。

sentences.en: They want to be talking about health care prices.
sentences.zh: 他们只想谈论医疗成本。

sentences.en: And what else could theoretically go wrong in this already theoretically complicated plan that Hakeem Jeffries has outlined?
sentences.zh: 在这个哈基姆·杰弗里斯已经概述的、理论上就很复杂的计划中，理论上还可能出什么问题？

sentences.en: Use the House to make economic case and build towards the midterms and then the presidential election.
sentences.zh: 利用众议院阐明经济立场，为期中选举以及随后的总统大选做准备。

sentences.en: Well, the biggest challenge is probably sorting out who is actually going to lead the party in 2020, that it's all well and good to have something on paper that says this is what
sentences.zh: 嗯，最大的挑战可能是弄清楚到底谁将在2020年领导这个党，纸面上有一份文件说明

sentences.en: the Democratic Party is, and this is some draft legislation that reflects that.
sentences.zh: 民主党是什么，并且有一些反映这一点的立法草案，这些都很好。

sentences.en: But at the end of the day, political parties are mostly defined by who they nominate for president.
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，政党主要由他们提名的总统候选人来定义。

sentences.en: And there is no guarantee at all that at this time next year, Democrats are going to be coalescing around someone who is talking about mainstream economic issues.
sentences.zh: 而且完全没有保证说，到了明年的这个时候，民主党人会团结在一个谈论主流经济议题的人周围。

sentences.en: So the House is trying to ignore the identity politics as phase one.
sentences.zh: 所以众议院在第一阶段正试图忽略身份政治。

sentences.en: But you're saying this could all go wrong if the future party leader, the nominee for president, doesn't do that.
sentences.zh: 但你的意思是，如果未来的党领袖、总统候选人不这样做，这一切都可能泡汤。

sentences.en: You can only put off the identity debate so long in that party.
sentences.zh: 在该党内，你只能把身份认同的辩论推迟那么久。

sentences.en: That's what happened on the Republican side.
sentences.zh: 共和党那边就是这样发生的。

sentences.en: They didn't want to talk about a lot of the identity issues and nationalism issues for years and years and years.
sentences.zh: 多年来，他们一直不想谈论很多身份认同和民族主义议题。

sentences.en: And ultimately, they end up with Donald Trump, someone who really did speak to the preoccupations of the party's most loyal, most fired up base.
sentences.zh: 最终，他们迎来了唐纳德·特朗普，一个真正说出了该党最忠诚、最热情的基层民众心声的人。

sentences.en: If Democratic voters feel that the party is giving them a set of options that are essentially
sentences.zh: 如果民主党选民觉得党内提供给他们的选择基本上是

sentences.en: boring or essentially non-confrontational and ducking the big issues that they want to be
sentences.zh: 乏味的、基本上不愿对立的，并且在回避他们想要讨论的重大议题，

sentences.en: talking about, that is how you end up nominating somebody totally out of left field, the Democratic
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么你最终会提名一个完全意料之外的人，也就是民主党

sentences.en: version of Trump, that if you present a choice between, you know, a Hillary Clinton versus
sentences.zh: 版本的特朗普，如果你在你知道的希拉里·克林顿和

sentences.en: Bernie Sanders, if Hillary Clinton were not a historic figure, that is probably how you end up with a candidate who compromises them in the general election.
sentences.zh: 伯尼·桑德斯之间做出选择，如果希拉里·克林顿不是一个具有历史意义的人物，这很可能就是你最终选出一个在全体大选中让他们妥协的候选人的方式。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Because you can only avoid talking about the elephant in the room for so long.
sentences.zh: 因为你对房间里显而易见的问题只能选择回避那么久。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And when you look at the candidates who are out there preparing most intensively for 2020, when you look at people like Joe Biden and Elizabeth Warren.
sentences.zh: 当你看看那些为2020年做最密集准备的候选人时，当你看看像乔·拜登和伊丽莎白·沃伦这样的人时。

sentences.en: Recently, a little bit coming up to me and they say, Kamala, talk to us about women's issues.
sentences.zh: 最近，有些人找到我，对我说：“卡玛拉，跟我们谈谈妇女议题吧。”

sentences.en: And I look at them and I say, I am so glad you want to talk about the economy.
sentences.zh: 我看着他们说：“我很高兴你们想谈论经济。”

sentences.en: Because what we know is when you lift up the economic status of women, you lift up the economic status of families and neighborhoods.
sentences.zh: 因为我们知道，当你提升女性的经济地位时，你就提升了家庭和社区的经济地位。

sentences.en: Kamala Harris and Cory Booker.
sentences.zh: 卡玛拉·哈里斯和科里·布克。

sentences.en: I remember talking to my grandfather about what it meant to get a job at a factory, at
sentences.zh: 我记得我跟祖父谈论过在工厂找到工作意味着什么，

sentences.en: Ford Motor Plant, the dignity of work.
sentences.zh: 在福特汽车厂工作，以及劳动的尊严。

sentences.en: Well, in one generation, we've destroyed that dignity of work, one, by commoditizing workers.
sentences.zh: 然而在短短一代人的时间里，我们摧毁了这种劳动的尊严，首先是通过将工人商品化。

sentences.en: You already see how careful they're being to really stay focused on the economy, but then try to figure out how can I also talk about the issues, the issues around immigration, the
sentences.zh: 你已经可以看到他们有多谨慎，以确保自己真正专注于经济，但随后又试图弄清楚我如何才能同时谈论那些

sentences.en: issues around law enforcement and social justice that rank and file Democratic activists demand that you talk about.
sentences.zh: 基层民主党活动人士要求你谈论的移民议题、执法和社会正义议题。

sentences.en: Who in your mind is the ideal person to realize this complicated alchemy that's involved in
sentences.zh: 在您看来，谁是实现这场长期博弈中所涉及的复杂炼金术的理想人选，即既要足够直接地谈论经济议题，

sentences.en: this long game of speaking directly enough to the economic issues, managing the expectations of the Democratic base, to talk about identity, with so many potential pitfalls?
sentences.zh: 又要管理民主党基层的预期去谈论身份认同，同时还要避开如此多的潜在陷阱？

sentences.en: Who is the right person?
sentences.zh: 谁才是合适的人选？

sentences.en: I think there are a lot of really prominent people in the party who are wrestling in an absolutely agonized way with that very question.
sentences.zh: 我认为党内有很多非常杰出的人物，他们正在极其痛苦地纠结于这个问题。

sentences.en: And what they're trying to figure out is not just what is the message, but what is the kind of person who can carry that message in a way that the country can hear?
sentences.zh: 他们试图弄清楚的不仅是传达什么信息，还有什么样的人能够以全国都能听进去的方式传递这个信息？

sentences.en: If they could sort of clone Barack Obama, that would be the person they would want to carry the message.
sentences.zh: 如果他们能克隆一个巴拉克·奥巴马，那就会是他们想要传递信息的人。

sentences.en: It's not clear that person exists right now.
sentences.zh: 目前还不清楚这样的人是否存在。

sentences.en: And so you end up having a conversation about how, well, if only Joe Biden were 20 years younger
sentences.zh: 所以你最终会进行这样的对话：如果乔·拜登年轻20岁就好了，

sentences.en: or if only Kamala Harris had been in the Senate for five years longer or something like that.
sentences.zh: 或者如果卡玛拉·哈里斯在参议院多待五年左右就好了。

sentences.en: And that's obviously not how you ultimately choose a presidential nominee.
sentences.zh: 显然，这并不是你最终挑选总统候选人的方式。

sentences.en: So the Democrats need another Barack Obama, but this time he would actually need to protect the party while in office.
sentences.zh: 因此，民主党需要另一个巴拉克·奥巴马，但这一次他实际上需要在任职期间保护党派。

sentences.en: They would need a sort of a Barack Obama with the wisdom of having governed for eight years as Barack Obama, right?
sentences.zh: 他们需要一个具备担任八年巴拉克·奥巴马总统执政智慧的巴拉克·奥巴马，对吧？

sentences.en: And that's not a person who's available.
sentences.zh: 而这样的人并不存在。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Thank you, Alex.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，亚历克斯。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 已解锁？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to The Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，你需要订阅《时报》才能访问所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你可以免费探索《时报》一个月，且无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download The New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》应用时，你在该应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，请立即下载《时报》应用并获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的内容。

sentences.en: You've met with the leaders of North Korea and Russia.
sentences.zh: 你已经会见了朝鲜和俄罗斯的领导人。

sentences.en: Are you prepared also?
sentences.zh: 你是否也做好了准备？

sentences.en: Are you willing to meet with President Rouhani?
sentences.zh: 你是否愿意会见鲁哈尼总统？

sentences.en: And under what conditions?
sentences.zh: 在什么条件下？

sentences.en: On Monday, just a week after threatening Iran with war in a tweet, President Trump said he would be willing to meet with the country's president, Hassan Rouhani.
sentences.zh: 周一，就在通过推特威胁对伊朗发动战争的一周后，特朗普总统表示他愿意与该国总统哈桑·鲁哈尼会面。

sentences.en: I do believe that they will probably end up wanting to meet, and I'm ready to meet anytime they want to.
sentences.zh: 我确实相信他们最终会想要会面，我随时准备在他们想要的任何时候会面。

sentences.en: And I don't do that from strength or from weakness.
sentences.zh: 我这样做不是出于实力，也不是出于软弱。

sentences.en: I think it's an appropriate thing to do.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一件合适的事情。

sentences.en: Such a meeting would mark the first face-to-face contact between the country's leaders since the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这将是自1979年美国与伊朗断交以来两国领导人之间的首次面对面接触，当时

sentences.en: severed diplomatic relations with Iran in 1979, after Iranian revolutionaries held 52 Americans hostage in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 伊朗革命者在美国驻伊使馆扣押了52名美国人作为人质。

sentences.en: embassy there.
sentences.zh: 那里的使馆。

sentences.en: Do you have preconditions for that meeting?
sentences.zh: 你对那场会面有什么前提条件吗？

sentences.en: No preconditions, no.
sentences.zh: 没有前提条件，没有。

sentences.en: They want to meet on me anytime they want.
sentences.zh: 他们随时都想和我见面。

sentences.en: Anytime they want.
sentences.zh: 随时都可以。

sentences.en: It's good for the country, good for them, good for us, and good for the world.
sentences.zh: 这对国家有益，对他们有益，对我们有益，对世界也有益。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》中，我们将为节日期间的招待做好准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让您的客宾宾至如归的妙招。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是遮光睡眠者吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们喝断片才能睡着。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们需要什么样的光线环境？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的要求。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 在《纽约时报》应用程序或您喜欢收听播客的任何地方搜索《Wirecutter秀》。
